gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify that the equality proposition asserts an if-and-only-if characterization, while the analysis proves only necessity and omits the converse showing that every admissible three-cluster configuration attains the claimed optimum.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The sufficiency direction of the equality characterization is unproved: clustered rows are derived from equality, but the reverse implication that the clustered construction achieves smallest singular value squared 1/n is not established.

component_coverage.gold_component: The claimed converse from the three-cluster configuration to attainment of the optimal smallest singular value is missing.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-001 explicitly states that only necessity is derived, that clustered configurations are not shown to attain 1/n, and supplies the cross-group calculation verifying attainment.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: Both identify the false lemma claim that pairwise non-collinearity of the three square vectors forces pairwise non-collinearity of their pair sums, and demonstrate that two pair sums can be collinear, causing repeated singular directions and invalidating the Case A inference.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: The lemma incorrectly infers pairwise distinct singular directions from pairwise non-collinear input squares; distinct input squares can have collinear pair sums, so the asserted all-three distinctness conclusion is false.

component_coverage.gold_component: The pairwise non-collinear square vectors need not have pairwise non-collinear pair sums, so the lemma's all-three distinct-direction conclusion is false.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-002 gives an explicit admissible counterexample with collinear pair sums, connects those sums to shared singular-vector directions, and states that the lemma and Case A strictness argument fail.

gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-002 recognizes that the one-argument arctangent loses the choice of which singular direction is first, but it does not recognize the separate domain failure that the quotient is undefined when its denominator is zero on an admissible input. The full gold concern therefore remains uncovered.
